per_task.question: What proportion of patients develop cytokine release syndrome after CAR T-cell therapy?
per_task.answer: The proportion of patients who develop cytokine release syndrome (CRS) after CAR T‑cell therapy varies widely across products and disease settings. In the pivotal pediatric B‑cell‑ALL trial of tisagenlecleucel, any‑grade CRS occurred in 77 % of treated patients[PMID:29385370]. A recent meta‑analysis that pooled data from many CAR T studies reported a pooled incidence of grade ≥ 3 CRS of 8 % (95 % CI 0.03–0.12) across the included trials[PMID:38696731]. Thus, while severe CRS is relatively uncommon (≈ 8 % in aggregate), overall CRS is frequent, affecting roughly three‑quarters of patients in some trials.
